references.text: Moses presents the same choice between blessing and curse for the people of Israel as a fundamental theme in Deuteronomy.
Moses repeats the choice between life and death, urging the people to choose life by loving the Lord.
God promises that whoever keeps His commandments shall live by them, linking obedience to life.
Ezekiel conveys God's desire that people turn and live, not die—the same theme of life and death as a consequence of choice.
Jeremiah conveys God's word about setting the way of life and the way of death before the people, directly parallel to Moses' words.
Proverbs confirm that the path of righteousness leads to life, while the way of sin leads to death.
Jesus speaks of the narrow and the broad way, leading respectively to life and destruction—the same twofold choice.
Paul contrasts the wages of sin, which is death, with God's gift, which is eternal life—the same contrast between life and death.
The one who sows in the flesh will reap corruption, but the one who sows in the Spirit will reap eternal life—the consequences of choice.
